title_en: Fengxiang Company v. Shanghai Salt Administration — dispute over administrative compulsory measures
keywords_en: administrative; administrative coercive measure; second instance; intermediate people's court; Shanghai municipality; legal person; state organ; Regulations on Salt Industry Administration; Measures for Administrative Enforcement of Salt Industry; Several Provisions of Shanghai Municipality on Salt Industry Administration; legality of administrative coercive measures; qualification of law enforcement subject; retroactivity of law; reversal of judgment; transport of industrial salt; administrative seizure; administrative litigation
full_text_en:
Fengxiang Company v. Shanghai Salt Affairs Bureau — administrative coercive measure dispute

Plaintiff: Shanghai Fengxiang Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Zhelin Town, Fengxian District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Jin Xuecai, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Defendant: Shanghai Salt Affairs Bureau, domiciled at: No. 2, Shimen Er Road, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Tang Qinghua, Director of the Bureau.

On May 21, 2001, the Shanghai Salt Affairs Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Salt Bureau) issued the coercive measure of seizure of salt-related illegal items under (Hu) Salt Administration [2001] No. 9, determining that Shanghai Fengxiang Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fengxiang Company) violated the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" by transferring industrial salt from other provinces and municipalities into this Municipality without the qualification to operate industrial salt. Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the "Measures for Administrative Enforcement of the Salt Industry," an administrative coercive measure was imposed on Fengxiang Company to seize a total of 300 tons of industrial salt. Fengxiang Company, dissatisfied, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai.

Plaintiff's Allegations: Our company, registered for industrial and commercial operations, holds the qualification to operate industrial salt. On May 11, 2001, we transferred 300 tons of industrial salt from Shandong. Due to transit time, the salt arrived in Shanghai on May 16. The Salt Bureau, however, seized the salt on the grounds that we violated the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration," which had not yet taken effect. Since that provision has no retroactive effect, the Salt Bureau's administrative seizure lacks legal basis. We therefore request the revocation of the seizure measure taken by the Salt Bureau.

Defendant's Defense: The "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" was promulgated on March 26, 2001, and came into effect on May 15, 2001. Fengxiang Company, aware of the content of that provision, violated it by transferring industrial salt into Shanghai after its effective date. Moreover, Fengxiang Company no longer holds the qualification to operate industrial salt. Our Bureau's seizure of the industrial salt illegally transferred by Fengxiang Company has a legal basis. We request that the seizure administrative act be upheld.

The Defendant Salt Bureau submitted the following factual evidence to the court:

1. Three cargo waybills of Jinan Railway Bureau, proving that the total weight of industrial salt dispatched from the First Salt Factory of Yangzi Town, Hanting District, Weifang City to Fengxiang Company was 180 tons, with the destination station being Shanghai Jinshanwei West Station, and the arrival date being May 16.

2. Two cargo waybills of Shanghai Railway Bureau, proving that the total weight of industrial salt dispatched from the Dingyuan County Salt Mine in Anhui Province to Fengxiang Company was 122 tons, with the destination station being Shanghai Jinshanwei West Station, and the arrival date being May 16.

The Salt Bureau used the above five cargo waybills to prove the illegal act of Fengxiang Company transferring industrial salt from other places into this Municipality.

The Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai found the following facts upon trial:

The Plaintiff, Fengxiang Company, transferred a total of 302 tons of industrial salt respectively from the First Salt Factory of Yangzi Town, Hanting District, Weifang City, Shandong Province and the Dingyuan County Salt Mine in Anhui Province, which arrived at Jinshanwei West Station of Shanghai Railway Bureau on May 16, 2001. The Defendant, Salt Bureau, determined that Fengxiang Company, without the qualification to operate industrial salt, arbitrarily transferred industrial salt from other provinces and municipalities into this Municipality, violating the relevant provisions of the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration." Consequently, on May 21, 2001, the Salt Bureau imposed on Fengxiang Company a coercive measure of seizure of salt-related illegal items and served the "Notice of Sealing Up and Seizure of Salt-Related Illegal Items" under (Hu) Salt Administration [2001] No. 9 on Fengxiang Company. Fengxiang Company, dissatisfied with the coercive measure, applied for administrative reconsideration to the Shanghai Municipal Commercial Commission. The Shanghai Municipal Commercial Commission, on August 21, 2001, issued an administrative reconsideration decision under Hu Shang Fu Jue Zi [2001] No. 1, upholding the seizure measure of the Salt Bureau.

The Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai held:

As the competent government authority, the Salt Bureau has the statutory power to investigate and handle salt-related illegal cases. The Salt Bureau's determination that Fengxiang Company transferred industrial salt from other provinces and municipalities into this Municipality was evidenced by cargo waybills, with clear findings of fact and conclusive evidence. Fengxiang Company's argument that its salt transfer act occurred before the implementation of the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" and thus the provision should not apply lacks merit: because Fengxiang Company's transfer of salt from other provinces into this Municipality was a continuing act, which should be deemed completed only upon the arrival of the goods in this Municipality. Since the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" had already come into effect at the time the act was completed, the Salt Bureau's application of that provision and the relevant provisions of the "Measures for Administrative Enforcement of the Salt Industry" to seize the industrial salt transferred into this Municipality by Fengxiang Company and to serve the seizure notice on Fengxiang Company was correct in law, and the enforcement procedure also complied with regulations, without impropriety.

Accordingly, the Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai, pursuant to Article 54, Item (1) of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," rendered the following judgment on December 29, 2001:

Sustain the administrative coercive measure of seizure of salt-related illegal items issued by the Shanghai Salt Affairs Bureau on May 21, 2001 under (Hu) Salt Administration [2001] No. 9.

After the judgment was pronounced, Fengxiang Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court.

Fengxiang Company's Grounds of Appeal: The first-instance judgment found unclear facts and improperly applied the law. Article 14, Paragraph 1 of the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" conflicts with Article 20 of the State Council's "Salt Industry Administration Regulations"; the appellant is not a party to a salt-related illegal case and therefore the relevant provisions of the "Measures for Administrative Enforcement of the Salt Industry" cannot apply; the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" does not apply to this case because the contract for the purchase of salt was formed before the implementation of that provision, so the provision has no retroactive effect on this case; even if it had retroactive effect, according to that provision, the Salt Bureau does not have the authority to investigate and handle industrial salt illegal cases. We therefore request the reversal of the first-instance judgment and a judgment revoking the Salt Bureau's administrative seizure measure.

The Salt Bureau argued: The first-instance judgment found clear facts and correctly applied the law. Our Bureau has the authority to investigate and handle industrial salt illegal cases; Fengxiang Company's illegal transfer of industrial salt into this Municipality was a continuing act, the completion of which occurred after the implementation of the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration," so that provision has effect on the appellant's illegal act. We request the dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the original judgment.

The Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court found the following facts upon trial:

Fengxiang Company had no objection to the first-instance court's finding that it transferred a total of 302 tons of industrial salt from other provinces and municipalities into this Municipality.

During the trial, the Salt Bureau provided the following legal basis to the court regarding its authority to seize illegally operated industrial salt:

1. Article 4 of the State Council's "Salt Industry Administration Regulations" provides: "The Ministry of Light Industry is the salt industry administrative department of the State Council, in charge of the national salt industry work. The salt industry administrative departments of provincial and sub-provincial people's governments shall be determined by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and shall be in charge of salt industry work within their respective administrative regions."

2. Article 7, Paragraph 1 of the Ministry of Light Industry's "Measures for Administrative Enforcement of the Salt Industry" provides: "Salt industry administrative departments at all levels shall establish salt administrative enforcement bodies responsible for salt administrative enforcement work within their respective jurisdictions."

3. Article 4, Paragraph 2 of the Shanghai Municipal People's Government's "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" provides: "The Shanghai Salt Affairs Bureau is the salt industry competent authority authorized by the Municipal People's Government pursuant to the 'Measures for the Exclusive Management of Edible Salt,' responsible for managing the exclusive management of edible salt within the administrative region of this Municipality, organizing the implementation of these Provisions, and subject to the leadership of the Municipal Commercial Commission."

In its cross-examination opinion, Fengxiang Company argued: Article 4, Paragraph 2 of the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" provides that the Salt Bureau is only responsible for "exclusive management of edible salt"; the Salt Bureau does not have the subject qualification for law enforcement regarding industrial salt operations; the Ministry of Light Industry's "Measures for Administrative Enforcement of the Salt Industry" is only a departmental rule and does not have the power to authorize the subject qualification for law enforcement.

The Salt Bureau argued: The "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" provides that the Salt Bureau is the salt industry competent authority authorized by the Municipal Government; the Salt Bureau has the authority to manage the exclusive management of both edible salt and industrial salt.

The Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court held:

According to Article 4 of the State Council's "Salt Industry Administration Regulations": "The Ministry of Light Industry is the salt industry administrative department of the State Council, in charge of the national salt industry work. The salt industry administrative departments of provincial and sub-provincial people's governments shall be determined by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and shall be in charge of salt industry work within their respective administrative regions." Article 7 of the Ministry of Light Industry's "Measures for Administrative Enforcement of the Salt Industry" provides: "Competent departments at all levels shall establish salt administrative enforcement bodies responsible for salt administrative enforcement work within their respective jurisdictions." Pursuant to the above regulations and rules of the State Council and the Ministry of Light Industry, the Shanghai Municipal People's Government formulated the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration," Article 4 of which provides: "The Shanghai Municipal Commercial Commission is the salt industry administrative department of this Municipality. The Shanghai Salt Affairs Bureau is the salt industry competent authority authorized by the Municipal People's Government pursuant to the 'Measures for the Exclusive Management of Edible Salt,' responsible for managing the exclusive management of edible salt within the administrative region of this Municipality, organizing the implementation of these Provisions, and subject to the leadership of the Municipal Commercial Commission." Therefore, the salt industry administrative department of this Municipality is the Municipal Commercial Commission, not the Salt Bureau. The Salt Bureau is only responsible for managing the exclusive management of edible salt and has no authority to investigate and handle the operation and transportation of industrial salt in this Municipality, nor does it have the subject qualification for law enforcement to make administrative coercive measures such as sealing up and seizing illegally operated industrial salt.

During the trial, the Salt Bureau provided the following legal basis for its specific administrative act:

1. Article 24 of the Ministry of Light Industry's "Measures for Administrative Enforcement of the Salt Industry" provides: "Where there is a possibility that a party to a salt-related illegal case may conceal or destroy evidence, the salt administrative enforcement body may seal up or seize the illegal items in advance and issue a notice of sealing up or seizure to the party."

2. Article 14, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" provide: "Salt other than edible salt and salt for the production of soda ash and caustic soda shall be uniformly operated by the Municipal Salt Company"; "Based on the principle of convenient supply, the Municipal Salt Company may entrust enterprises holding edible salt wholesale licenses to sell salt other than edible salt and salt for the production of soda ash and caustic soda; any unit or individual not so entrusted shall not sell such salt without authorization."

During the second-instance trial, the Salt Bureau failed to provide factual evidence that Fengxiang Company had a "possibility of concealing or destroying evidence."

Fengxiang Company argued that it had the right to operate industrial salt, and that it was neither a party to a salt-related illegal case nor had any situation of concealing or destroying evidence, so the circumstances described in Article 24 of the "Measures for Administrative Enforcement of the Salt Industry" did not apply to it. According to Article 20 of the State Council's "Salt Industry Administration Regulations," the wholesale business of salt shall be uniformly operated by salt companies at all levels. In places where no salt company is established, it shall be uniformly organized and operated by units authorized by the people's government at or above the county level. Article 14 of the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" conflicts with Article 20 of the State Council's "Salt Industry Administration Regulations."

The Salt Bureau argued that the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" does not conflict with the relevant provisions of the "Salt Industry Administration Regulations," and according to the reply content of the letter Zhong Yan Zheng [2000] No. 109 from the Salt Industry Administration Office of the State Bureau of Light Industry, "Reply to the Shanghai Salt Affairs Bureau's Request for Interpretation of 'The Wholesale Business of Salt Shall Be Uniformly Operated by Salt Companies at All Levels'," the Municipal Salt Company uniformly operates salt products including industrial salt, and other units and individuals shall not engage in the procurement and distribution of uniformly operated salt products.

The Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court held:

The Salt Bureau failed to provide factual evidence that Fengxiang Company had a "possibility of concealing or destroying evidence," therefore, the Salt Bureau's application of Article 24 of the "Measures for Administrative Enforcement of the Salt Industry" to impose the coercive measure of seizing industrial salt on Fengxiang Company constituted unclear findings of fact and improper application of laws and regulations. Article 19 of the State Council's "Salt Industry Administration Regulations" provides: "Edible salt, state reserve salt, and salt for the production of soda ash and caustic soda under state mandatory plans shall be uniformly allocated and transferred by the state." This case involves industrial salt, which does not fall within the category of salt subject to uniform allocation and transfer by the state as stipulated in the above provision. Article 20 of the "Salt Industry Administration Regulations" provides: "The wholesale business of salt shall be uniformly operated by salt companies at all levels. In places where no salt company is established, it shall be uniformly organized and operated by units authorized by the people's government at or above the county level." According to the business scope of Fengxiang Company's business license, Fengxiang Company has the business scope for operating industrial salt and is a company that can operate industrial salt and has the right to operate industrial salt. Therefore, the Salt Bureau's specific administrative act based on Article 14 of the "Several Provisions of Shanghai on Salt Industry Administration" constituted improper application of laws and regulations. According to Article 31 of the "Salt Industry Administration Regulations," these Regulations shall be interpreted by the Ministry of Light Industry. The document Zhong Yan Zheng [2000] No. 109, "Reply to the Shanghai Salt Affairs Bureau's Request for Interpretation of 'The Wholesale Business of Salt Shall Be Uniformly Operated by Salt Companies at All Levels'," provided by the Salt Bureau, is a document from the Salt Industry Administration Office, an internal organ of the State Bureau of Light Industry. The Salt Industry Administration Office of the State Bureau of Light Industry has no authority to interpret the "Salt Industry Administration Regulations," and moreover, that reply letter was not publicly announced, so it has no legal effect externally.

In summary, the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court held:

In this case, the Salt Bureau failed to provide factual evidence that Fengxiang Company violated relevant edible salt management regulations, and moreover, it does not have the subject qualification for law enforcement to seal up or seize industrial salt. The Salt Bureau's administrative coercive measure of seizing Fengxiang Company's industrial salt had unclear findings of fact and erroneous application of laws and regulations; the specific administrative act was unlawful. The first-instance court's judgment upholding the specific administrative act constituted unclear findings of fact and erroneous application of laws and regulations. Fengxiang Company's appeal request should be supported. Accordingly, the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 54, Item (2), Subitems 1 and 2 and Article 61, Item (3) of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," rendered the following judgment on May 24, 2002:

1. Set aside the administrative judgment under (2001) Jing Xing Chu Zi No. 71 of the Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai;

2. Set aside the administrative coercive measure of seizure of salt-related illegal items issued by the Shanghai Salt Affairs Bureau on May 21, 2001 under (Hu) Salt Administration [2001] No. 9.

The case acceptance fees for the first and second instances, totaling RMB 200, shall be borne by the Shanghai Salt Affairs Bureau.
